title: CRITICAL: a run expires its own dispatch lease during boot and hard-stops itself
description:
Measured on run_d941c5ee: lease acquired 08:31:19, gateway token issued 08:31:24, token revoked 08:32:26 with reason stopped:hard, and the harness first real model call returned 403 run_token_revoked. Nobody asked for a stop.

Cause: runs.ts acquireDispatchLease is called with no ttl_ms, so it takes DEFAULT_LEASE_TTL_MS = 60s. The Workflow then boots the sandbox (clone, toolchain, model probe, harness probe, pre-flight — about 60s here) and only renews the lease at the FIRST OBSERVATION, which is behind step.sleep(pollDelay) = 15s more. So the first renewal happens at roughly boot + 15s, always later than the 60s it was given, and renewDispatchLease answers lease_lost. detectTrip treats a lost lease as a HARD trip, which since gyl revokes the gateway token immediately.

This is almost certainly what the $49.80 runaway actually was. Before gyl a lost lease ended the pass and the next attempt booted and minted a fresh token, forever — a reboot loop that spends, which matches 892 calls with nothing ever finishing. gyl turned an infinite spend loop into an immediate self-kill; neither is the intended behaviour.

Fix both halves: acquire the lease with a ttl that covers a cold boot (image pull included), and renew it as soon as the sandbox is booted, before the first poll sleep. Neither alone is sufficient — a long boot outlives any fixed acquire ttl, and a renewal that only happens after the first sleep is always too late.

Add a regression test that a boot slower than the lease ttl does not produce a lost lease, driving the real Workflow rather than asserting on the constants.
